Definition: from G5093; to prize, i.e. fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere:--honour, value.
BiblicalUsage: Honour, in this word, is something you give where it is due. God commands it to father and mother, Paul repeats the command in Ephesians 6:2, Peter tells believers to honour all men, to love the brotherhood, to fear God and honour the king, and Jesus promises that the Father will honour the one who serves Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that honour is not flattery but recognition: it sees the worth God has placed on a person or a command and answers it with respect. I believe a church that honours well — parents, rulers, one another, and above all God — shows the world what reverence looks like in practice.
